subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests within one reviewer/run, and what cache key and outcome scope are acceptable?
rationale: Exec auto-review participates in process execution approval, so replacing one fresh model review per request with a cached verdict needs explicit approval-boundary intent even though the cost bug is source-reproducible.

options.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
options.body: Cache only within the reviewer/run using the full reviewed input or prompt as the key, with tests and real configured-run proof before merge.

options.title: Require broader host coverage
options.body: Block the candidate PRs until direct node-host and plugin helper paths either reuse reviewer lifetime or are explicitly documented out of scope.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated model cost to preserve one fresh model-backed approval review per exec request.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
recommendation.body: Cache only within the reviewer/run using the full reviewed input or prompt as the key, with tests and real configured-run proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: joshavant introduced the normalized exec auto-review behavior and is the strongest feature-history owner for the cache semantics decision.
